c-ci-growth.label: Compound interest is repeated multiplication
c-ci-growth.summary: Each year the amount is multiplied by the same factor (1 + r/100). So times and powers move together.

c-si-line.label: Simple interest is a straight line
c-si-line.summary: Interest = P × r × t ÷ 100. With several loans at one rate, add P × t for each and divide once.

q-ci-multiple.label: How long to grow k times?
q-ci-multiple.summary: It triples in 6 years; how long to become 27 times?

q-ci-find.label: Principal or rate from two amounts
q-ci-find.summary: A sum becomes A₁ after n years and A₂ after n + 1 years; find the rate or the principal.

q-ci-fractional.label: Compound interest for years and months
q-ci-fractional.summary: 2 years 9 months with annual compounding: compound the whole years, simple interest on the rest.

q-si-two.label: Simple interest on two loans at one rate
q-si-two.summary: Two principals for different times, total interest known; find the rate.

q-si-basic.label: Basic: interest, rate, time or principal
q-si-basic.summary: Three of P, R, T and the interest are given; find the fourth. Includes day counts, equal-interest pairs and rupee-years.

q-si-multiple.label: A sum becomes k times itself
q-si-multiple.summary: Doubles in n years; find the rate or the time to become 3, 4 or 5 times. Also interest as a fraction of the sum.

q-si-difference.label: Extra interest from a higher rate
q-si-difference.summary: A rate 2% higher (or one more year) gives Rs. X more; the extra interest is a percent of the principal.

q-si-parts.label: Money split into parts at different rates
q-si-parts.summary: A sum lent in parts at different rates; find a part, a missing rate or the average rate.

q-si-amounts.label: Amounts given, find principal or rate
q-si-amounts.summary: The amount after one time and after another (or a ratio of P : A) is given; the gap between them is the interest.

q-ci-basic.label: Basic compound interest: amount, interest or sum
q-ci-basic.summary: Find the amount, the compound interest or the sum; includes changing rates by year and the matching simple interest.

q-ci-diff.label: Difference between compound and simple interest
q-ci-diff.summary: The gap between CI and SI for 2 or 3 years is known; find the sum or the rate. Also with half-yearly compounding.

q-ci-half.label: Compounded half-yearly or quarterly
q-ci-half.summary: Halve (or quarter) the rate and double (or quadruple) the number of periods; also yearly versus half-yearly and years-and-months.

q-ci-install.label: Loans repaid in equal instalments
q-ci-install.summary: A loan repaid in two equal yearly instalments: the instalments, discounted year by year, add up to the loan.

q-ci-growth.label: Population, price or value growth
q-ci-growth.summary: A value grows or falls by a fixed percent each year: multiply by (1 ± r/100) once per year.

q-ci-multiple.cue: 'It triples (or doubles) in n years. When will it become k times?'
q-ci-multiple.standard: Triples in 6 years. 27 = 3 × 3 × 3, so three tripling periods: 3 × 6 = 18 years.
q-ci-multiple.fast: Write the target as a power of the growth factor (27 = 3³) and multiply the time by the power.
q-ci-multiple.eliminate: The answer is a whole multiple of 6, so only the option that is a multiple of 6 survives (18 of 18, 19, 20, 21).
traps: Taking 27 ÷ 3 = 9 and then 9 × 6 = 54, treating growth as simple.
Adding instead of multiplying (6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24).

q-ci-find.cue: Two amounts at consecutive years (7,200 after 2 years and 8,640 after 3).
traps: Dividing by 1.2 once instead of twice.
Using the 3-year amount with 2 years of growth.

q-ci-fractional.cue: Time like 2 years 9 months, 'interest compounded annually'.
q-ci-fractional.eliminate: Two full years alone give about ₹1,997 (12,000 × 0.1664), and 9 more months add about 6% of ₹14,000 ≈ ₹840. That is just under ₹2,840, so only 2,837 fits.
traps: Compounding the 9 months as (1.08)^(9/12).
Using simple interest for all 2 y 9 m.
Computing 9 months as 9% instead of 6% (8% × 9/12).

q-si-two.cue: Two loans (or investments) at the same simple-interest rate and one total interest.
q-si-two.eliminate: Even at 10%, 26,000 'rupee-years' would give ₹2,600. The actual ₹2,000 is lower, so the rate must be below 10%: only 8% fits.
traps: Dividing by total principal 10,000 instead of rupee-years (gives 20%).
Using the years separately instead of P × t.

q-si-basic.cue: 'Find the rate / time / principal / interest' with plain numbers, or two loans at one rate.
q-si-basic.standard: Rate = SI × 100 ÷ (P × T). For two deposits add the rupee-years first: 400 × 2 + 550 × 4 + 1,200 × 6 = 10,200, so 1,020 ÷ 10,200 = 10%.
q-si-basic.fast: Turn R × T into one percent of P and cancel: 30% of 6,000 = 1,800 at once.
q-si-basic.eliminate: Estimate the answer's size first: interest ÷ principal gives R × T, and the options usually differ by whole steps.
traps: Leaving months or days unconverted (6 years 8 months is 6 2/3 years).
Counting both end dates in a day-count (the first day is not counted).
Dividing by the total principal instead of the rupee-years.

q-si-multiple.cue: 'Doubles / trebles in n years' or 'SI is 1/4 of the sum'.
q-si-multiple.standard: Trebles in 15 years means interest 2P in 15 years, so P every 7.5 years. 5 times needs 4P: 4 × 7.5 = 30 years.
q-si-multiple.fast: Each 'P of interest' takes the same time. Doubles in n: k times in (k − 1)n.
q-si-multiple.eliminate: Time for k times is (k − 1) multiples of the doubling time, so the answer must be a multiple of it.
traps: Taking trebles as 3 × the time (it is 2 × the doubling time).
Using the amount, not the interest, as the multiple.
When SI = P/4 and T = R: r² = 25, so r = 5, not 25.

q-si-difference.cue: 'Had the rate been x% higher it would have fetched Rs. … more' or 'the difference in interest is …'.
q-si-difference.standard: 3% extra for 2 years = 6% of P = 72, so P = Rs. 1,200.
q-si-difference.fast: Multiply the rate gap by the years and read it as a percent of the sum; divide the money gap by it.
q-si-difference.eliminate: The answer must make the extra percent × P equal the gap exactly, so test one option.
traps: Using the old rate instead of the gap.
Forgetting to multiply by the years.

q-si-parts.cue: 'Divided into two parts / lends part at … and rest at …'.
q-si-parts.standard: Equal interest on two parts: P₁ × (R₁T₁) = P₂ × (R₂T₂), so P₁ : P₂ = R₂T₂ : R₁T₁. For 12,000 split at 3 y 12% and 4.5 y 16%: 72 : 36 = 2 : 1, so 8,000 and 4,000.
q-si-parts.fast: The parts are inversely proportional to rate × time. For an average rate use weights (alligation).
q-si-parts.eliminate: The larger part belongs to the smaller R × T.
traps: Writing the ratio the wrong way round.
Forgetting the second part's fraction is of the remainder (50% of the rest).

q-si-amounts.cue: 'Amounts to … in … years and … in … years' or 'ratio of principal and amount is …'.
q-si-amounts.standard: 880 after 2 years, 920 after 3: interest per year = 40, P = 880 − 2 × 40 = 800.
q-si-amounts.fast: Subtract the two amounts to get interest per year; take away the earlier years' interest to reach P.
q-si-amounts.eliminate: P is always smaller than the smaller amount by (years × yearly interest).
traps: Taking the later amount as the principal.
Dividing the gap by the later time instead of the time difference.

q-ci-basic.cue: 'Find the amount / compound interest / sum'; rates that change each year; 'CI is … find the SI'.
q-ci-basic.standard: Chain the yearly multipliers: 10,000 × 1.04 × 1.05 × 1.06 = 11,575.20, so CI = 1,575.20. CI for 2 years at 5% is 10.25% of P; use it to get P and then the SI.
q-ci-basic.fast: Memorise 1.05² = 1.1025, 1.1² = 1.21, 1.1³ = 1.331, 1.2² = 1.44, 1.05³ = 1.157625. CI ÷ factor gives P, and the SI is just rate × years of P.
q-ci-basic.eliminate: SI for the same sum is always a little less than the CI; the amount is always above the sum, the interest is not.
traps: Giving the amount when the interest is asked (6,655 for 1,655).
Adding the yearly rates instead of multiplying the factors.
Using the 2-year factor as 1 + 2r.

q-ci-diff.cue: 'The difference between compound and simple interest for 2 (or 3) years is Rs. …'.
q-ci-diff.fast: 2 years: the difference is the interest on the first year's interest, r% of one year's interest. 3 years at r%: P (3r² + r³).
q-ci-diff.eliminate: Try one option: for 2 years at r% the difference is exactly P × r²/10,000.
traps: Using the 2-year formula for 3 years.
Writing r as a percent in the formula (use 0.05).
Mixing the sign: CI is the larger.

q-ci-half.cue: 'Compounded half-yearly / quarterly / semi-annually', or 'for 1 1/2 years' and '2 years 4 months'.
q-ci-half.standard: 20% quarterly for 9 months: rate 5%, 3 periods. 1.05³ − 1 = 0.157625, so CI = 16,000 × 0.157625 = 2,522. For a time like 2 years 4 months at 15% yearly: 8,000 × 1.15² = 10,580, then × (1 + 0.15 × 4/12).
q-ci-half.fast: Recognise the factor: 1.157625 = 1.05³ means 3 periods at 5%; the number of periods gives the time.
q-ci-half.eliminate: Half-yearly gives a slightly larger amount than yearly at the same rate (not smaller).
traps: Halving the rate but not doubling the periods.
Using the annual rate for each half-year.
Compounding the leftover months instead of simple interest on them.

q-ci-install.cue: 'Repaid in two equal annual instalments' at compound interest.
q-ci-install.fast: To check an option, divide it by 1.05 once and twice and add. For a loan L: x = L × (1.05)² ÷ (2 + 0.05) = L × 1.1025 ÷ 2.05.
q-ci-install.eliminate: Two instalments must add to more than the loan but less than loan × 1.1025.
traps: Dividing the loan by 2 (ignores the interest).
Applying one year's factor to both instalments.
Using the same factor for the first and second payment.

q-ci-growth.cue: 'Value depreciates by 4% every year' / 'population increases by …'.
q-ci-growth.standard: Depreciation multiplies by (1 − r/100) each year: 62,500 × 0.96² = 57,600.
q-ci-growth.fast: 62,500 × 0.96 = 60,000, then 60,000 × 0.96 = 57,600. Go forward by multiplying, backward by dividing.
q-ci-growth.eliminate: Two falls of 4% take off a little less than 8% in all (7.84%), so the value is just above 92% of 62,500 = 57,500: only 57,600 fits.
traps: Subtracting 8% in one step.
Using 1.04 instead of 0.96.
